newsitem.title: GERMANY: German motor insurers speed up accident reporting.
newsitem.headline: German motor insurers speed up accident reporting.

text.p: German motor insurers have reorganised their central telephone hotline for accident victims, centralising activities in Hamburg and making the system much faster, the insurance federation Gesamtverband der Deutschen Versicherungswirtschaft (GDV) said in Hamburg.
The service was introduced in 1972 and is used annually by around 500,000 motor accident victims, because the driver causing the accident does not know the name of the insurer.
Claimants who have the registration of the other car involved in the accident are given the name and phone number of the insurer.

"Until now, we relied on the vehicle registration centres," Volker Sonnenburg of GDV said. "This was slow and time-consuming. We are now creating our own database with all 50 million vehicles in Germany, their registration and insurer."
The database already contains 40 percent of all cars and would be complete by mid-1997, Sonnenburg added. All 127 motor insurers active in Germany supplied data and kept them up-to-date.
The Hamburg call centre, which is equipped with 90 telephone lines and 35 work stations, can also connect claimants directly with many insurers' claims handling services.
The nine existing regional GDV call centres will be closed this year. Instead of regional numbers, one central phone number (0180 25026) is now in place. Costs per call are 0.12 DM, said Sonnenburg.
Insurers expect considerable savings from the move. "Until now, we had to pay four DM per inquiry or two million DM annually to the registration office," said Sonnenburg.
But the main benefit would be felt by individual insurers. "Fewer than half of the motorists causing an accident report within a week to their insurer," said Sonnenburg.

With the new system, insurers can establish contact with claimants much faster and avoid unnecessary expenses, he said. The average motor third-party liability claim costs 5,500 DM, of which an estimated 300 DM could be saved through early contact, he said.
